gitar-v2.text: The new BROKER_PUBLIC clause added to LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() is also used by IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate() to filter already-linked brokers, causing users to be unable to re-authenticate with their linked broker when the IDP has an organizationId without kc.org.broker.public=true

getLoginSearchOptions() built from values() has no BROKER_PUBLIC entry while getLoginPredicate() now includes it, contradicting the LoginFilter javadoc that the enum contains all fields considered for login availability
Test cleanup uses literal 'alias' instead of the actual alias 'idp-alias-<i>', causing all 21 identity providers to leak and persist across test methods
Leaked IDPs from testCacheIDPByOrg become realm-level login IDPs after organizations are deleted, causing testCacheIDPForLogin assertions to fail when test order varies

remove() method calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) unconditionally even when the provider is already in the realm cache, causing an unnecessary DB round-trip when the cached CachedIdentityProvider already holds the needed model

Removed foundProviders.size() > 1 guard allows ambiguous classpath with equal-order crypto providers to silently pick arbitrary provider instead of failing fast, potentially causing FIPS deployment to run on non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider
Dead ASN1Encoder.write() calls on lines 114-115 in concatenatedRSToASN1DER create throwaway instances and discard results, causing unnecessary allocations and misleading readers
Adding order() as abstract method to CryptoProvider interface breaks external implementations - should be a default method for source and binary compatibility
ES384/ES512 tests use default P-256 key instead of proper curve sizes (secp384r1/secp521r1), so tests only verify zero-padding round-trips rather than actual signature handling
Ignored-provider StringBuilder is built unconditionally even when debug logging is off, and result is passed as format string to logger.debugf() which could cause issues with % characters
JS UI English messages for error-invalid-multivalued-size were rewritten from i18next syntax ({{0}}) to Java MessageFormat ({0}), breaking interpolation in account-ui and admin-ui bundles
Diff-range computation in verifySafeHtml can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when common-prefix and common-suffix lengths overlap
Lithuanian translation for TOTP step 1 was replaced with Italian text instead of Lithuanian
Traditional Chinese text was placed in zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) account bundle for totpStep1 instead of Simplified Chinese
Missing English sibling file causes build to abort with raw RuntimeException instead of readable verification error
Anchor mismatch error message in santizeAnchors omits key and file name, making it impossible to locate the offending entry
isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong character offsets (substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6)) for reading the grant type shortcut from the 6-character encoded prefix
isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition - returns false when substring equals expected shortcut instead of when it doesn't match
AccessTokenContext null-check on line 73 validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to be accepted

New abstract getShortcut() method on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI interface breaks existing third-party grant providers with AbstractMethodError at startup - should be a default method returning null for backward compatibility

hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) only falls back to the all-clients resource when no client-specific resource is found, so an admin with all-clients manage/configure/map-roles permission is denied on client X when any single-client permission exists for X - should evaluate both resources as a union instead of mutually exclusive

getClientsWithPermission returns 'Clients' literal string instead of actual client ids because per-client resources don't have type set, causing NPE when consumer calls realm.getClientById on bogus id
getResourceName method not extended for new Clients resource type, causing client permission resources to fall through to resource.getDisplayName() which is never set, yielding null name
getEvaluationContext method is private and never called, along with unused logger, Scope import, and TOKEN_EXCHANGE import - dead code that should be removed
Duplicated scope-matching loops in hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String) and hasGrantedPermission should be factored into single helper

Permission cleanup listener is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1) which stops cleanup for realms with leftover v1 policies when no FGAP feature is enabled, leaving orphaned policies - should gate on !ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 instead

UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with zero arguments, but the only declaration in the hierarchy is UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) - this does not compile and causes the services module to fail to build

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) returns false when user == null, so on normal first-time login (no user set in context) webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is never invoked, causing passkeys autocomplete and webauth form to disappear from the initial login page
Operator docs claim rolling-updates feature must be enabled or operator will fail, but operator code never enforces this feature gate - the update logic works with the feature disabled

UpgradeTest skips feature enablement for null-strategy case - the updateStrategy == null branch returns before the FeatureSpec/ROLLING_UPDATES block, so parameterized runs with default strategy deploy without the preview feature
setEnabledFeatures overwrites existing list instead of appending - calls setEnabledFeatures(List.of(ROLLING_UPDATES)) which discards any features already declared in the base deployment YAML
printFeatureDisabled hardcodes the feature key string 'rolling-updates' instead of using Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey(), causing potential drift if enum is renamed

User-storage recovery codes are never consumed / reusable - after logging in with code #1 the same code still validates on the next login because nothing in the flow tells the storage which code was consumed, and createFromValues regenerates a full unused 12-code model on every call

Optional.get() in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean can throw NoSuchElementException - credentialModelOpt.get() is called with no presence check, causing a 500 error when getCredential() returns empty for providers that don't override CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials

getCredentials() NPEs when user is absent from provider map - the new getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without the null check that sibling methods perform, causing NPE instead of returning empty stream

Recovery codes in user storage cannot be disabled/removed - disableCredentialType only handles OTP and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream only reports OTP, so deleting recovery-codes credential logs success but the credential remains and user can keep authenticating

V2 canManage() grants manage on a view-only Groups permission - GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an admin holding only an all-groups permission with the view scope passes the check, allowing them to create top-level groups when they should only have view access

V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs instead of group IDs - per-group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource never get a type set, so resourceStore.findByType only visits the schema's own all-groups resource and skips every group-specific resource

V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes groupResource.getId() (the resource UUID) into hasPermission which looks resources up by name, causing lookup misses and returning non-existent group IDs that break user search filters

Dropped global-view short-circuit re-evaluates policies per group - filter(groupsEvaluator::canView) runs the full check for every group in the page instead of hoisting canView() into a local variable, causing N policy evaluations instead of one

getResourceName has no branch for the new Groups resource type - group resources are created with a name equal to the group ID and no display name, so a group scope permission falls through to resource.getDisplayName() and surfaces as null instead of the group path or 'All groups'

Returning null from getSubGroupsCount breaks its documented contract - GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() is documented as 'Never returns null' but the new branch returns null for concurrently deleted groups, causing the admin UI to treat it as 'has subgroups' instead of zero

Test asserts before joining reader thread, so it can pass with the bug - assertThat runs immediately after deletedAll.set(true) without joining the reader thread, allowing exceptions from in-flight requests to be added after assertion is evaluated
Test catches Exception but not Throwable/Error from the reader thread, so those are never observed

New test creates 100 groups without registering realm cleanup - if fail() fires during creation or any remove() throws, the already-created groups stay in the class-scoped realm and leak into following test methods

Null guard added only to getSubGroupsCount; sibling paths still NPE - the three getSubGroupsStream() overloads at lines 256/262/268 dereference modelSupplier.get() unguarded and will still produce NPE for concurrently deleted groups

isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for spawn processes because SpawnProcess does not subclass the default context's Process class, causing process.kill() to never be called for hung processes, leading to process leaks, Redis connection leaks, and potential duplicate segment production to Kafka
The same incorrect isinstance check in join() means terminate() never runs for spawn processes
_create_process_for_shard method is defined but never called anywhere in the codebase - dead code that should be removed
join() breaks out of the loop when deadline is reached, so remaining processes never reach the terminate() call and are not proactively terminated during timed shutdown

In runShardSplitQuery the expr/hide filters now run before interpolation, so a target whose variable resolves to an empty string is not dropped, causing requestSupportsSharding to return false and form its own otherQueries group, leading to runSplitGroupedQueries hitting requests.filter(...)[0].partition with an empty requests array and throwing a TypeError

runShardSplitQuery interpolates targets, then hands each sharded sub-request to runSplitQuery which interpolates them again, causing applyTemplateVariables to be called multiple times per target and resulting in duplicated ad hoc filters being appended for non-indexed labels

New tests mock templateSrv.replace to rewrite $__auto to 5m, but the real applyTemplateVariables destructures __auto out of scopedVars so $__auto stays literal for backend resolution, meaning the test assertions encode behavior the shipped code does not produce

getUserPermissions no longer reads permCache, causing every Check that the cached scope map does not satisfy to fall through to a full DB query, resulting in N sequential DB permission queries when a user browses N dashboards they cannot see
Denial cache is only populated and never invalidated, so once a Check is denied the user keeps getting Allowed: false for the full 30s TTL even if permissions are granted in the meantime
userPermDenialCacheKey joins action, name and parent with underscore, but UIDs can legally contain underscores, causing key collisions between different resources
userPermDenialCacheKey uses raw checkReq.UserUID instead of resolved userIdentifiers.UID, causing user:1 and user:<uid> for the same person to get separate cache entries
Test for deny-cache precedence seeds permission cache with false value instead of true, so the test passes even without the denial cache being consulted
permission_cache_usage metric reports denial-cache hits as cache_hit=true while genuine permCache hits that resulted in deny are reported as cache_hit=false, making the hit ratio meaningless
Removing the cache hit test case leaves cacheHit false in every remaining case, making the if tc.cacheHit seeding and require.Equal(t, 1, store.calls) assertion unreachable
New behaviour where getUserPermissions must always re-query the store even when permCache is populated is untested

FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and reused for every strategy, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate()/join() call queue_pool.shutdown(), which permanently kills the pool. After a rebalance, the new strategy submits into shut-down queues with dead workers, causing silent data loss as messages are dropped and offsets committed.

OffsetTracker state (last_committed, outstanding, all_offsets) persists across create_with_partitions() calls. After a rebalance where a partition is revoked and later reassigned, stale last_committed values prevent offsets from being committed again, and stale outstanding entries leak memory.

commit() is invoked from a background commit_thread instead of the main arroyo consumer loop, causing concurrent access to shared consumer/commit-policy state and potential commits for already-revoked partitions. The _commit_loop also swallows all exceptions making failures invisible.

Queues are unbounded (created without maxsize) and submit() never raises MessageRejected, so there is no backpressure despite the docstring claiming 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up'. This can cause consumer OOM with slow subscription groups.

FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets worker.shutdown = True before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False), causing workers to exit before draining queued items. join(timeout) also ignores its timeout parameter.

test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts test_partition not in committed_offsets but the implementation calls complete_offset in the worker's finally block even when processor raises, so the assertion only passes due to timing (commit loop's 1s tick hasn't fired yet).
metrics.incr for offsets_committed increments by len(committable) which is the number of partitions, not the actual number of offsets committed, under-reporting by orders of magnitude.
TotalDocs() iterates b.cache map without cacheMu lock while BuildIndex writes the map under cacheMu.Lock(), causing fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' crash
Index-build goroutines race on shared err variable and unsynchronized totalBatchesIndexed++ counter when WorkerThreads > 1, causing data race and incorrect span attributes
NewResourceServer leaks context and goroutines when eager Init fails - cancel() is not called on failure path, leaving background context and started work running
Eager init ignores caller context - Init runs on internally created context.Background()-derived ctx, making startup index build uncancellable during shutdown

Trace-propagation fix incomplete - bleve.BuildIndex, ListIterator, WriteEvent, and ReadResource still use '_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)' instead of 'ctx, span := ...', leaving new spans childless

enableSqlExpressions computes enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions) and then returns false on both branches, making the toggle read have no effect and lines 133-138 of ReadQuery unreachable dead code
enableSqlExpressions has inverted negation relative to its name - a maintainer changing the second return false to return enabled/true will enable SQL expressions exactly when the flag is off

Legacy SQL path (nodes.go -> UnmarshalSQLCommand -> NewSQLCommand -> sql.TablesList) fails with misleading 'invalid sql' error instead of stating the feature is disabled, because the new gate only exists in ReadQuery
go.work.sum lines 891-892 still contain github.com/scottlepp/go-duck v0.3.1 hashes even though go.mod/go.sum dropped this dependency

Write lock lacks double-check pattern - with cold cache in non-dev mode, N concurrent requests all read ret == nil under RLock, then queue on write lock and each one re-opens and re-parses assets-manifest.json before overwriting cache, causing N sequential disk reads plus JSON decodes instead of one
RLock/ret read at lines 41-43 is dead work in Dev mode since the condition short-circuits on cfg.Env
Cleanup ticker dropped from 10m to 1m, causing all eight cleanup jobs to run 10x more often than before, adding extra DB load and increasing concurrency window - appears to be a debug leftover
Six new r.log.Error calls fire on every cleanup batch logging entire fetched ID slices at ERROR severity for successful routine operations, flooding logs and triggering alerting
Quadratic string building for SQLite inline ID list using fmt.Sprintf in a loop reallocates and copies the whole accumulated string on each iteration, causing gigabytes of copies per batch
deleteByIDs placeholder limit only handled for SQLite; MySQL and Postgres cap at 65535 bound parameters but cleanupjob_batchsize is never bounded, causing cleanup to fail with driver errors
Test cleanup registered after setup assertions can leak rows - if assertion fails, FailNow aborts before cleanup is registered, leaving rows behind and causing cascading failures in later subtests

Migration crashes when embed_category site setting is absent - execute(...)[0]['id'] is evaluated unconditionally and raises IndexError/NoMethodError on empty PG::Result when no row exists in site_settings

update/destroy raise NoMethodError on unknown host id - EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil for non-existent id, causing host.host or host.destroy to raise NoMethodError instead of returning 404
before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil - self.host.sub! is called before format validation runs, so EmbeddableHost.new.save raises NoMethodError instead of validation failure

record_for_host is case-sensitive - URI host returns mixed case but query uses lower(host), so uppercase hostnames never match, causing InvalidAccess in EmbedController and TopicRetriever rejecting valid embeds

Plural hydration assumes array and drops unresolvable ids - m[2] branch calls obj[k].map() without checking value is an array, throwing TypeError for null or scalar values, and deletes id key unconditionally leaving undefined values

New host row shows empty category after save - saving without touching category chooser sends category_id: null, server substitutes uncategorized_category_id but component sets category from null resulting in blank category badge
Migration interpolates setting value into SQL unescaped - host strings from embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into INSERT VALUES, allowing SQL injection via single quotes
Fabricator file contents are swapped between the two files - category_fabricator.rb contains embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains category fabricators

expandable_first_post? spec no longer tests what its name claims - after dropping embeddable_hosts.present? check, the example 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false
store test requests fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1's colors - test calls store.find('fruit', 2) but asserts colors from fruits[0], passing only because pretender ignores id and always returns fruits[0]
PUT /admin/customize/embedding and saveChanges are dead no-ops - Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing and saveChanges action is not bound to any control in embedding.hbs

I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale, so non-controller paths like Sidekiq jobs, notification emails, and post_destroyer run with fallback locales' YAML never loaded, causing 'translation missing' errors instead of fallback strings
The accelerator caches the frozen missing-translation string for the process lifetime when fallback locales aren't loaded

The fallback chain depends on SiteSetting.default_locale which is per-database in multisite, but the accelerator's LRU cache key doesn't include site or default_locale, causing cross-site cache pollution where one site's fallback translation is served to another site
Cache staleness occurs after an admin changes default_locale until the process restarts because there's no cache invalidation on setting change

Async legacy writes inherit request context and get cancelled - all four write paths spawn goroutines with context derived from request context, which gets cancelled when handler returns, causing legacy writes to abort with context.Canceled
Mode 3 integration tests silently run as mode 1 - SetDualWritingMode defaults to Mode1 and only implements Mode1<->Mode2 transitions, so Mode3 falls through and returns Mode1

Wrong histogram used for several duration recordings - storage failures in Create and Update are recorded into legacy histogram, and legacy DeleteCollection records into storage histogram with startLegacy
Delete passes object name as the kind metric label instead of options.Kind, creating unbounded Prometheus label cardinality
Delete puts the unenriched logger (d.Log) into the context instead of the enriched log variable with name/kind/method values

Update no longer sends the storage-updated object to legacy - raw objInfo is passed to Legacy.Update instead of updateWrapper with the already-computed result, causing potential divergence between stores
Mode 3 tests never verify the async legacy write - tests return immediately without awaiting the goroutine, so legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection calls are never verified
deleteCache handler fetches full credential row including encrypted key field instead of selecting only the id needed for ownership check
deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError, resulting in 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of proper 404 NOT_FOUND response
Cache status bypasses the calendar-cache feature flag by instantiating CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of using CalendarCache.init() factory
updateManyByCredentialId({}) is a dead write that issues unnecessary UPDATE queries on every cache refresh with empty data payload
test-gcal-webhooks.sh uses BSD/macOS sed syntax (sed -i '') that fails on Linux GNU sed
test-gcal-webhooks.sh writes to ../.env relative to working directory instead of script location, causing .env to be created outside the repo
test-gcal-webhooks.sh cleanup function always exits 0 even on tunnel failure, masking errors from callers and CI
dev:cron script switched to npx tsx but tsx is not listed as a dependency, causing ad-hoc downloads and offline/CI failures
Cache timestamp is hardcoded to en-US locale instead of using user's locale preference
Disconnect action no longer checks isDelegationCredential for delegation credential ids, allowing actions that will fail server-side
deleteCache mutation has no isPending guard, allowing duplicate submissions when rapidly confirming
remove_member bypasses counter cache by using group.users.delete(user_id) which uses delete_all strategy, leaving groups.user_count stale and not clearing users.primary_group_id
Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI, making members 51+ unreachable
Adding an existing member causes 500 error due to unique group_users index violation because add_members doesn't check for existing membership
totalPages calculation uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 causing off-by-one error that creates phantom empty last page when member count is exact multiple of page size
members endpoint accepts unbounded/negative limit and offset parameters without server-side validation, causing PostgreSQL errors or allowing serialization of entire membership
add_members 500s when usernames parameter is sent as an array instead of comma-separated string because it calls .split() on the array
members specs still assert removed array JSON shape and remain pending, providing no coverage for new {members:, meta:} contract; remove_member spec uses wrong HTTP verb (:put instead of :delete)

Delete and Pause menu items unreachable in the new list view - AlertRuleMenu gates Pause on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) and Delete on rulerRule && but rulerRule is undefined in the new list view path since ruler request was removed

Silence menu item is a no-op for prom-only rules - canSilence is true for Grafana prom rules but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only renders when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) and rule is undefined, so clicking Silence does nothing

skipToken yields permissive abilities instead of all-false - useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) computes loading === false so Duplicate/View/Explore return [true, permission] instead of [false, false], incorrectly showing Duplicate for cloud rules

Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView list - GrafanaRuleLoader was rendered with key={key} but replacement GrafanaRuleListItem has no key prop, causing React reconciliation issues in infinite-scroll list
Rule view links lose returnTo parameter breaking back navigation - new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo query param that was used to restore previous list/filter state when navigating back
Stray '// duplicate' comment left in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities at line 289 with no meaning for readers

MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated because it extends StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of the four abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), causing TypeError when any metric_alert_fire detector reaches process_detectors
Assigning an abstract class to detector_handler: type[DetectorHandler] | None is a mypy type-abstract error

TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds expected occurrence with wrong group key - build_mock_occurrence_and_event uses 'val1' but the call under test evaluates group key 'group_key', causing fingerprint mismatch and test failure
Test fixtures use hard-coded value of 6 where packet values are 10/8/100, which only passes because the mock ignores value - should assert on real arguments to cover the new hook's value passthrough
evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list but the return type changed to dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]

Team permission check ANDs isTeamAdmin with isTeamOwner, reducing the branch to owner-only since isTeamAdmin already returns truthy for both ADMIN and OWNER roles. A team ADMIN who is neither the booking's organizer nor an attendee gets FORBIDDEN. It also fires two queries with teamId ?? 0 for personal bookings.

Guest emails are not normalized: blacklistedGuestEmails is lower-cased but guest is not, so submitting Blocked@Example.com passes the includes filter and bypasses the blacklist. Same case sensitivity issue applies to existing-attendee check.
Server schema has no uniqueness refine for guest emails (only the client does), so a direct tRPC call with duplicate emails inserts multiple attendee rows for the same person.

Handler ignores eventType.disableGuests flag, allowing organizer/attendee of a disableGuests: true event type to add attendees through the mutation, bypassing the constraint the booking page enforces.

sendAddGuestsEmails skips disableStandardEmails checks - it takes no eventTypeMetadata and sends unconditionally, so event types configured with disableStandardEmails.all.host/attendee will still email everyone when a guest is added.

Emails are keyed off raw input instead of uniqueGuests - sendAddGuestsEmails receives the unfiltered input while only uniqueGuests were actually inserted, causing existing attendees to receive wrong email notifications.
No booking status/time validation before adding guests - handler only checks permissions, not booking.status, so CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings can still get new attendee rows via direct tRPC call.
isInvalidEmail state is never reset on success - after a failed validation sets isInvalidEmail, reopening the dialog shows the error banner over an empty form.
MultiEmail imports @calcom/ui from inside packages/ui, creating a circular dependency cycle index.tsx → MultiEmailLazy → MultiEmail → index.tsx.
New organizer email uses APP_NAME instead of EMAIL_FROM_NAME, causing inconsistent sender name for deployments that customize the sender name.

Light-theme args swapped in desktop/topic-post.scss .topic-meta-data h5 a - lightness went from 30% to 70%

mobile/user.scss .name had $primary lightness 30% but was converted to 50%, losing intended contrast
mobile/topic-post.scss h3 had $primary lightness 20% but was converted to 50%, no longer matching desktop/topic-post.scss:321's 20%/80%
.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification in _topic-list.scss left unconverted with bare scale-color($primary) while six other rules in same file were converted

retryCount delete branch is not scoped to method SMS - the new retryCount > 1 branch sits in an OR with no method constraint, so this SMS-only cron issues a table-wide delete of every WorkflowReminder whose retryCount exceeds 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows

Throwing update inside catch aborts the whole cron run - the prisma.workflowReminder.update added inside the catch block is unprotected and if the row was removed between findMany and this update, Prisma throws P2025 which escapes the for-loop and fails the whole handler
website_name attribute bypasses untrusted_attributes gating for TL0 users, exposing host and path information that should be hidden for spam-link protection
include_website_name guard method is incorrectly named (should be include_website_name? with question mark) so active_model_serializers never calls it and defaults to true
website_name should be added to the untrusted_attributes list and the hand-written include_website_name method should be deleted
website_name should be added to the spec's untrusted attribute list at line 11
String literal mutated via << operator in discourse_host.ends_with?(".".<<(website_host)) will cause deprecation warning on Ruby 3.4 and FrozenError when frozen string literals are enabled
Domain match logic is asymmetric - instance example.com with website www.example.com/user hides path, but instance forums.example.com with website example.com/user shows it
Domain match logic incorrectly matches unrelated sites sharing public suffixes (e.g., forum.github.io and someone.github.io would match and show full path)
Should normalize leading www. and compare registrable domains rather than using raw label counts for domain matching

Feature-flagged table widget renders hardcoded empty data - tableResultComponent passes empty columns and tableData instead of actual result.data and result.meta when use-table-widget-visualization flag is enabled

field query param can crash summarize endpoint with a 500 - process_raw_response uses request.query_params.getlist('field') which causes KeyError when invalid field is passed, and silently strips error_ids when legitimate field is used

fetch_error_details mispairs error_ids with nodestore payloads - zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes get_multi returns dict in same order as input, but it doesn't maintain order and omits missing events
One unrecognized report type discards the whole browser report batch - returning 422 on first invalid report drops all sibling reports in the batch instead of skipping invalid ones

age/timestamp mutual exclusion bypassed by falsy 0 and by omitting both - validate_timestamp and validate_age use truthiness check instead of is not None, allowing both fields with value 0 or neither field to pass validation

Attribute-keys request silently stopped filtering by environment - removed useApiQuery sent environment parameter but makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions omits it, causing users to get attribute keys from all environments

Migration to useQuery drops retry:false and omits org from cache key - new useQuery doesn't set staleTime, refetchOnWindowFocus, or retry options, and queryKey lacks organization slug causing potential cross-org cache collisions

Custom cell renderers returning null/0/'' fall through to the default - renderers check if (cell) instead of cell !== undefined, causing intentional null/0/empty string returns to trigger fallback renderer
_handle_regex_match is now dead code in parametrize_w_experiments - removing ParameterizationRegexExperiment left the nested closure defined but never referenced

In get_monitor_environment_context the local config copy is built and its schedule_type replaced with the human-readable display value, but the returned dict uses monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of config. Every occurrence event therefore ships schedule_type as the raw integer (e.g. 1) rather than "crontab"/"interval", and the copy is dead code. Return the mutated copy.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result ({ success, data }), but the Google service assigns that whole object to key and persists it, corrupting the credential so that subsequent googleCredentialSchema.parse throws and the Google Calendar credential becomes permanently unusable

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] which evaluates to literal string '[object Object]', causing the schema to strip expiry_date/expires_in, instance_url, scope, token_type, and overwrite the real refresh_token with the literal string 'refresh_token'

refreshOAuthTokens returns raw fetch Response to non-fetch consumers (Google expects Gaxios result, HubSpot expects HubspotToken object), causing TypeError for Google and NaN expiryDate plus credential destruction for HubSpot
refreshOAuthTokens never checks response.ok, so an error page from the sync endpoint is parsed as a token

Salesforce getClient performs unconditional refresh-token request on every service instantiation without expiry check, persists new key, but still builds jsforce.Connection from old access_token/instance_url, discarding the freshly obtained token
Webhook uses prisma.credential.findFirst which picks one row non-deterministically when a user has multiple credentials for the same app, potentially overwriting the wrong account's tokens
Webhook returns 500 on malformed/missing body instead of 4xx because appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throw is not caught
Webhook returns 500 when symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse throws due to wrong encryption key or non-JSON plaintext instead of returning 4xx
Webhook has no HTTP method check, so a GET request with the right header reaches the parse and returns 500
Webhook secret is compared with !== which short-circuits on first differing byte, creating a timing side channel vulnerability since the endpoint is unauthenticated and unrate-limited

Legacy box-model fallbacks in new mixins are incomplete/incorrect - flexbox() emits display: -moz-box but align-items() emits no -moz-box-align, -ms-align-items is not a real property, values passed untranslated for legacy syntax, and -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group are 1-based so order(0) emits invalid value

Float/clearfix leftovers are inert now containers are flex - .contents still carries clearfix class creating extra zero-size flex items, and .small-action's clear: both plus .topic-avatar { float: left } are no-ops inside flex container

Date-override day bypasses the busy check entirely - when a host has any date override on the slot's UTC day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true at the if (dateOverrideExist) short-circuit and never reaches the busy.every(...) loop, allowing double bookings

Inverted find() rejects slots covered by another range - both loops treat 'this entry does not contain the slot' as 'the slot is unavailable', causing valid slots to be rejected when multiple override ranges exist on one date or with split schedules

Working-hours check computes end from the slot start time instead of slotEndTime - const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute() duplicates the start expression, so slots that overrun working hours are incorrectly allowed

Overrides crossing invitee midnight produce zero slots - startTime/endTime rebuilt from hour()*60 + minute() after adding offset silently wraps at midnight, causing buildSlots to emit nothing for cross-midnight overrides
dayjs objects compared with === so the branch is dead - comparing two distinct dayjs object references is always false, so the 'unavailable all day' override case (start === end) is never handled

Override day comparison uses server-local formatting instead of UTC - dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format() formats in server's local zone while slotStartTime.format() is UTC, causing day strings to disagree near midnight
AssignmentSource.queued default uses timezone.now() which is evaluated once at import time, not per instance creation, making the timestamp useless for staleness/expiry decisions
Test test_to_dict only asserts queued is not None, which passes even with the frozen timestamp bug - should assert timestamps differ between instances created at different times
assignment_source parameter added to sync_status_outbound but no caller passes it and overrides don't declare it, making it dead code that could cause TypeError if used

TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger() instance instead of the receiver, causing logs to be recorded on a throwaway logger and making test assertions fail (InfoLogs.Calls will be 0 instead of expected value)

ContextualLoggerMiddleware is missing the ordering invariant documentation that was present on the deleted InstrumentationMiddleware, and is registered third in the middleware stack instead of first - any future middleware inserted above it that calls logger.FromContext(ctx) will silently lose pluginId/endpoint/dsUID/uname attributes
Test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after the middleware was renamed to MetricsMiddleware - should be renamed to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the new type

One failing SendGrid cancel blocks all cron cancellations - the cron's cancel loop wraps every client.request call and Promise.all in a single try/catch, so if any SendGrid request throws, reminders queued after the failing one are never processed and no cancelled reminders are deleted
Reschedule uses immediateDelete which takes the direct POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends path that fails once 100 pending cancellations accumulate, letting stale reminders fire for rescheduled bookings

immediateDelete email path never deletes the WorkflowReminder row - the branch cancels the SendGrid send and returns without deleting or updating the WorkflowReminder record, leaving orphaned rows in the database

<%- end if %> in best.html.erb raises a SyntaxError - the header block closes with invalid Ruby syntax that compiles to 'end if ; ...' which has no predicate, causing template compilation failure when rendering best view
poll_feed crashes on RSS items with no content - calling .scrub on i.content which is nil for feed items without content/description element raises NoMethodError and aborts entire feed poll

Weak postMessage origin check uses substring match - discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 accepts any message whose origin is a substring of the configured Discourse URL rather than comparing origins exactly

Unescaped request.referer injected into inline script - raw referer interpolated into single-quoted JS string literal without escaping, allowing referer containing single quote or </script> to break out of string/context
Migration adds force: true to create_top_topics - will silently DROP existing top_topics table and its data if migration is re-run or run on DB where table already exists

upsampled_count() drops events with null sample_weight - the ifNull(sample_weight, 1) wrapper was removed, so events without client-side sampling contribute 0 instead of 1 to the total, causing charts to silently under-report error volume

60s eligibility cache is stale, unkeyed on option, and never invalidated - cache key only uses org id and hash of project_ids, so changes to issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist take up to a minute to reflect, and hash() collisions between different project sets could apply wrong verdict
invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code with no call site and no option-update hook
Accidental gitlink 'sentry-repo' committed without .gitmodules entry, causing fresh clones and git submodule update --init to fail or warn

upsampled_count declares default_result_type='number' instead of 'integer', causing response meta to report float type for an integer series and different chart formatting than ordinary count() results

Column transform duplicated across three branches - identical transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling calls in three places means future branches added to _get_event_stats will silently miss the transform
New caching and invalidation paths have no test coverage - is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects cache-hit branch and invalidate_upsampling_cache are never executed in tests

getBaseConditions can return top-level OR without parentheses - when there are no filters, authConditions is returned verbatim without enclosing parentheses, causing SQL precedence issues when combined with additional predicates that could return bookings outside authorized scope
getFilterConditions returns bare OR conditions without parentheses when only eventTypeId is set, causing SQL precedence issues

Widened options type lets invalid scope/teamId combos silently match nothing - constructor takes InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions instead of discriminated union, so invalid combinations like { scope: 'team', userId, orgId } with no teamId type-check but cause safeParse to fail, silently degrading to 1=0 condition
Unreachable else if (filterConditions) and final else branches in getBaseConditions since authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object
Dead code in reduce callbacks - if (index === 0) return condition is unreachable because reduce without initial value starts at index 1
Filter-only branch in getBaseConditions would return filter conditions with no authorization predicate if it ever became reachable
Caching tests deleted while cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions memoization logic is retained, leaving the undefined vs null sentinel path for getFilterConditions untested

EmailValidator calls record.errors[attribute] which in Rails 3.2 inserts an empty array for missing keys, causing user.errors.to_hash to always contain an email key after validation runs, leading to valid emails being permanently rejected in the signup form when other validation errors occur

BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact case-sensitive where(email: email) lookup without downcasing, allowing blocked emails to be bypassed with trivial case variations like Spammer@Mail.com instead of spammer@mail.com

match_count double-counts because UsersController#create calls both user.valid? and user.save which re-runs validations, and since should_block? mutates state (match_count += 1, last_match_at), a single blocked signup attempt increments match_count by 2
OptimizedCursorPaginator uses int keys on a datetime order_by field, causing TypeError when build_cursor calls math.floor on a datetime object, resulting in 500 errors
OptimizedCursorPaginator's value_from_cursor returns raw int to build_queryset, producing invalid 'datetime <= <int>' SQL predicate
Negative-offset slicing with enable_advanced_features=True raises Django ValueError (500) on user-supplied cursors like '1700000000000:-5:0' instead of returning 400
organization_context.member can be None for token auth, causing AttributeError on member.has_global_access access and turning working audit-log GET into 500
Advanced pagination is incorrectly gated on has_global_access which is set for ordinary members in open-membership organizations, not just admins
request.user.is_superuser bypasses superuser session elevation, should use is_active_superuser(request) instead
BasePaginator silently clamps negative offsets for forward cursors but still 500s for prev cursors with negative offsets, creating inconsistent behavior
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result, causing future maintenance divergence
No tests cover the new OptimizedCursorPaginator class or the new endpoint branch
Comment in cursors.py:26-28 advertises negative-offset support that is not actually implemented

KeyError on metadata["sender"]["login"] breaks reconnect flow with HTTP 500 because sender key is not always present in integration metadata - build_integration only sets it when state.get("sender") is present, and ensure_integration replaces metadata wholesale on pipeline finish

OAuth state parameter uses pipeline.signature which is a public constant (md5 of pipeline view class FQNs), providing no CSRF/replay protection - an attacker can trivially supply the correct state in a forged callback
get_user_info raises requests.HTTPError on non-2xx responses, causing unhandled 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed error page

User match validation is skipped when Integration row doesn't exist yet - when Integration.objects.get raises DoesNotExist, the view returns pipeline.next_step() with no validation, allowing an attacker to complete install into their own org

Inconsistent status filter between first and second Integration lookup - first lookup has no status filter while second requires status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE, causing non-ACTIVE integrations to fail with wrong error message

test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found because it passes a mismatched state value, causing OAuthLoginView to short-circuit before reaching the stubbed 404 on /app/installations/{id}

Unguarded destructured destinationCalendar crashes EventManager.create - `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined when event has no destination calendars, and line 119 reads `.integration` on it without optional chaining, causing TypeError when booking a Google Meet event for users without destination calendars

Google update/delete destinationCalendar fallback always resolves undefined - in both updateEvent and deleteEvent the fallback branch searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` when externalCalendarId is already falsy, so it can never match and always returns undefined, causing updateEvent to fail and deleteEvent to silently fall back to 'primary'

events.patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId in createEvent - selectedCalendar is undefined when no destination calendar matches credentialId, and while insert call guards with `selectedCalendar || 'primary'`, the follow-up calendar.events.patch passes raw selectedCalendar, causing Google Meet booking patches to fail

Collective host calendars dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null - `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when event type and organizer both have no destination calendar, silently discarding collective co-hosts' calendars

referencesToCreate loses video credentialId - `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops credential id for non-calendar (video) results, breaking handleCancelBooking's ability to pick the exact video credential

referencesToCreate loses calendar externalId - branches for destinations without credentialId and the 'first connected calendar' fallback call createEvent without externalId, storing null where they previously stored the destination's externalId, breaking later update/delete targeting

Recurring cancellation deletes each event once per calendar reference - the recurring/allRemainingBookings block was moved inside the per-reference loop but doesn't use reference at all, causing duplicate deleteEvent calls for collective bookings with multiple calendar references
TopicUser.find_by returns nil for users without a topic_users row, causing a crash when calling tu.notification_level on nil at line 107

State-changing GET unsubscribe action is CSRF-vulnerable and prefetchable since check_xhr is skipped and no confirmation step exists, allowing third-party pages or mail clients to silently mute topics
Logged-out users clicking the unsubscribe link are silently redirected to homepage with no message and nothing unsubscribed due to rescue_from Discourse::NotLoggedIn behavior

Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping - notifications_reason_id stays at old value, notifications_changed_at is not bumped, and no notification_level_change message is published to MessageBus
topic.set('details.notificationReasonText', null) targets a getter-only computed property with no setter, so the cached reason text value remains and is still rendered
No spec covers the new topics#unsubscribe action - nil TopicUser crash, watching→regular vs regular→muted transition, and slug redirect are all unverified

Backup-code login skips password verification if totpCode is sent - an attacker with a leaked backup code can bypass password check by sending any junk totpCode value, reducing 2FA to single factor authentication
Dismissing backup-codes step via Escape/outside click leaves 2FA switch stale - server-side 2FA is enabled but UI shows disabled, and reopening modal shows stale backup codes screen

Empty backup code submit on login gives no user feedback - form has noValidate so required/minLength attributes are inert, and submitting empty backupCode silently re-enters 2FA state without error message
missing_backup_codes message points users to non-existent settings UI - users who enabled 2FA before migration have no way to generate backup codes as instructed
Non-string backupCode in disable request causes 500 TypeError - calling replaceAll on unvalidated JSON input throws TypeError instead of returning 400 error
Copy button reports success even when clipboard write fails - navigator.clipboard.writeText promise is not awaited or caught, showing success toast unconditionally

Local cache is set before store write in tagDeviceUI, allowing the device limit to be bypassed - cache entry is present after first rejection so subsequent requests short-circuit the cache check and authentication succeeds while device is never persisted

rowsAffected==0 conflates 'unchanged row' with limit reached - MySQL reports affected rows as changed rows not matched rows, so a device tagged twice within the same second produces 0 changed rows and legitimate existing devices are refused authentication
wire.go still registers ProvideAnonDBStore with no int64 provider - the store is now built inside ProvideAnonymousDeviceService but wire.go still has stale registration that will fail wire generation
New device_limit option missing from defaults.ini, sample.ini, and docs - operators cannot discover the option and Grafana's convention of having every setting in defaults.ini is broken
ErrDeviceLimitReached is a plain fmt.Errorf so device-limit rejection is logged as auth error with no user feedback - user sees generic login/401 with no indication the anonymous device limit was hit
Loss of panic recovery when tagging moved into auth path - the removed goroutine wrapped TagDevice in recover() but tagging now runs inline so a panic propagates into authentication middleware

30-day expiration constant duplicated across three files (api/api.go, anonstore/database.go, impl.go) - future changes to expiration window will silently desynchronize counting, listing and limit enforcement

Frontend anonymousDeviceLimit typed as optional (number | undefined) but backend DTO field is non-pointer int64 so payload always contains a number (0 when feature is off) - consumers treating undefined as 'no limit configured' will instead receive 0

Duplicate self.downsize definition silently shadows the 4-arg form - the width/height form at 145-147 is immediately redefined by the dimensions form at 149-151, making the first definition dead code and causing TypeError when callers use the old signature

Hardcoded 10MB limit bypasses per-type upload size settings - client-side validation uses blanket 10*1024 KB while server enforces max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb per type, causing mismatched validation and incorrect error messages

Animated GIF originals flattened to first frame when allow_animated_thumbnails setting is off - the downsizing loop uses a thumbnail setting for originals, causing convert to take only the first frame and lose animation

Downsize loop runs ImageMagick convert over SVG uploads - FileHelper.is_image? matches svg, so large SVGs are rewritten by convert, replacing vector source and causing upload.images.size_not_found errors

Downsize loop ignores failures and re-runs ImageOptim up to 5 times - the loop discards OptimizedImage.downsize's boolean result, so when convert fails the same failing command runs five times before rejection

AttributeError on every audit-log request when member is None - enable_advanced is computed unconditionally and organization_context.member can be None, causing AttributeError when accessing has_global_access for org auth token/API key auth requests

OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime key - get_item_key calls math.floor on a datetime object instead of using DateTimePaginator's multiplier-based conversion, causing TypeError on non-empty pages

Negative cursor offset reaches Django slice and raises ValueError - Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets which Django rejects with ValueError instead of BadPaginationError, causing unhandled 500 errors

Admin-only pagination gate accepts any org member - OrganizationMember.has_global_access defaults to True and request.user.is_superuser is checked instead of is_active_superuser(request), allowing ordinary members to access the feature

set->zset switch reuses span-buf:s: keys causing WRONGTYPE on rollout - sadd/sscan/sunionstore/scard replaced with zadd/zscan/zunionstore/zcard but key format unchanged, causing WRONGTYPE errors during rolling deploy
max_segment_spans constructor parameter is now dead code - the only consumer was removed from _load_segment_data while Lua hardcodes 1000, so configured values are silently ignored

Redirect-chain loop bound reduced from 10001 to 1001 iterations with warning comment removed - traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 now silently split into separate segments with no documentation of the limit

Offset clamp in BasePaginator is half-applied - prev-cursors still use raw offset so crafted cursors with negative offsets cause 500 errors, and comments incorrectly claim Django handles negative slicing

async callback in forEach escapes try/catch - the surrounding try/catch in reschedule.ts files can never catch failures from getCalendar/deleteEvent because the callback returns a promise that nobody holds, causing rejected calendar deletes to surface as unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged

In bookings.tsx the external calendar/video deletions are only scheduled - the mutation returns and in a serverless runtime the invocation can be frozen before deleteEvent/deleteMeeting is even issued

import() calls in object literal load every app eagerly - appStore stores the result of import() so all 28 app packages start loading when @calcom/app-store is evaluated, defeating the PR's goal of not pulling in all apps
Any app whose module-level code throws produces a rejected promise that nobody awaits until that key is accessed, causing an unhandled rejection at startup rather than a catchable import error
